# blob_url { #labdata.github.blob_url }

```python
labdata.github.blob_url(owner, repo, commit, path, directory=False)
```

Build a stable URL for one version of a published file.

The URL names the commit rather than a branch, so it keeps pointing at the
bytes that were cataloged rather than at whatever the branch holds later.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**owner**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository owner.

<code>[**repo**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository name.

<code>[**commit**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Commit sha of the version.

<code>[**path**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository-relative path.

<code>[**directory**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [False]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Whether `path` is a dataset held in a directory, which has a page rather than a download.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   A URL to the content, or to the directory listing for a dataset.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
blob_url("munch-group", "tree-stats", "7701707", "results/dummy.csv")
# 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/munch-group/tree-stats/7701707/results/dummy.csv'
```
